opensociety.w: George Soros's grant-making network, named after Karl Popper's idea of the open society; it spent $1.2 billion in 2024, almost $700 million of it in grants, and $24.2 billion since it began (Devex). Its arts giving began in the Soros Center for Contemporary Art, opened in Budapest in 1985 as a documentation centre, and grew from 1992 into a network of about twenty Soros Centers for Contemporary Art across Central and Eastern Europe, the former Soviet Union and Central Asia (Budapest, Prague, Warsaw, Moscow, Kyiv, Sarajevo, Almaty and others), which ran exhibitions, catalogues and training before being spun off as independent organisations in 1999 and 2000. The foundation's stated reason is that art and culture carry open-society values and shape public attitudes, yet get too little recognition and money from governments, so its Arts and Culture Program set out to build an independent, innovative arts sector and to change cultural policy where states controlled culture; its culture team today puts it as art being an essential driver of social change. Later programmes followed the same line: the Documentary Photography Project and its Moving Walls shows, the Soros Arts Fellowship for socially engaged artists (from 2018; $100,000 unrestricted to each of 18 fellows in 2023), a $15 million four-year initiative from 2019 to speed the restitution of African objects after France's Sarr-Savoy report, and a $180,000 grant in 2024 to The Africa Institute in Sharjah for a fellowship on African heritage and repatriation. Critics, among them Octavian Esanu (“the managed avant-garde”) and Aaron Moulton (“The Influencing Machine”), read the centres as having set a Western-facing agenda for post-socialist art. Alexander Soros took control in June 2023; the network then cut about 40 per cent of its staff, closed offices from Kampala to Almaty and folded its programmes into four areas (climate justice, equity, expression, justice). National foundations in the network (Kosova Foundation for Open Society, the Open Society Initiative for West Africa, FOKAL in Haiti, the Mongolian Foundation for an Open Society) are counted here under the one network; several were closed or given a final package in 2024.
